  • Trip point - a temperature where the system acts: passive = slow down, critical = shut down. See: srs-items.
  • TSC (Time Stamp Counter) - Time Stamp Counter; a CPU counter that rises at a fixed rate and is the fastest clock for the OS when stable. See: linux-os, processors.
  • TTL - Time To Live, the number of router hops a network packet may still make. See: tools.
  • TTY - A terminal or serial device in Linux (ttyS0, ttyUSB0, pts/0). See: buses-1.

U

  • UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter) - The chip behind a serial port, e.g. 16550A. See: buses-1.
  • UAS (USB Attached SCSI) - USB Attached SCSI: the faster protocol for USB storage; the older one is Bulk-Only Transport (usb-storage). See: buses-2, graphics, storage.
  • udev - The Linux device manager; it names devices, creates /dev/disk/by-* links and keeps a database of device properties. See: buses-1, linux-os, storage.
  • UDP (User Datagram Protocol) - a simple send-and-forget protocol used by DNS, games and voice. See: network.
  • UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) - Unified Extensible Firmware Interface; the modern firmware that replaced the PC BIOS. See: linux-os, machine.
  • UEFI variable - a named setting stored in the firmware's flash, such as BootOrder or SecureBoot. See: machine.
  • UID (user ID) - the number the kernel uses for a user account; the name is only a label. See: linux-os.
  • UMC (Unified Memory Controller) - AMD's memory controller, built into the CPU's Data Fabric. See: buses-1, machine.
  • UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) - A battery unit that keeps the PC powered during a power cut. See: sensors.
  • USB (Universal Serial Bus) - The common peripheral bus: 1.5 and 12 Mbps (USB 1), 480 Mbps (USB 2), 5/10/20 Gbps (USB 3.x). See: buses-1.
  • usb.ids - the community list that maps USB vendor and product numbers to names, installed by the hwdata package. See: buses-2.
  • USB/IP - a Linux feature that shares USB devices over the network; its virtual host controller is vhci_hcd. See: buses-1, buses-2.
  • USB4 - the newest USB standard (up to 40 or 80 Gbps) that can tunnel PCI Express and DisplayPort. See: buses-2.
  • usbfs - the Linux interface that lets a user program talk to a USB device directly instead of through a kernel driver. See: buses-2.
  • UUID (Bluetooth service) - Universally Unique Identifier: an ID stored in a filesystem, used to mount it reliably. See: network, storage.

V

  • VA-API (Video Acceleration API) - The Linux interface for hardware video decoding and encoding. See: graphics.
  • VBIOS - The graphics card's own firmware chip. It starts the card at power-on and holds its power and clock tables. See: graphics.
  • VCN / UVD - AMD's video decode/encode engine. VCN is the current name; some chips still report it as UVD. See: graphics.
  • Vcore - the main supply voltage of the CPU cores, measured by the motherboard's sensor chip. See: processors.
  • vDSO - a small piece of kernel code mapped into every program so that reading the clock does not need a real system call. See: tools.
  • Vendor ID - The 16-bit number that names a chip maker, e.g. 1022 AMD, 1002 AMD/ATI, 10EC Realtek. See: buses-1.
  • Vendor library (GPU) - the GPU maker's own tuned maths library: hipBLAS (AMD ROCm), cuBLAS (NVIDIA CUDA) or CLBlast (OpenCL). See: tools.
  • VID - Voltage Identification; the voltage the CPU requests from the regulator. See: processors.
  • VID / PID (Vendor ID / Product ID) - the two 16-bit numbers that identify a USB device's maker and model, written VVVV:PPPP. See: buses-2.
  • VID:PID - USB vendor ID and product ID, which identify a USB chip or device model. See: storage.
  • VKD3D-Proton - A translation layer that turns Direct3D 12 calls into Vulkan, used by Proton. See: graphics.
  • VMD - Volume Management Device: an Intel PCIe block that gathers NVMe drives for Intel RST and VROC. See: storage.
  • VPN (virtual private network) - an encrypted tunnel that carries your traffic through another network or server. See: network.
  • VRAM - The graphics card's own fast memory. See: graphics.
  • VROC - Virtual RAID on CPU: Intel's RAID for NVMe drives attached to the processor. See: storage.
  • VRR (variable refresh rate) - The monitor waits for the GPU's next frame instead of refreshing at a fixed rate. Sold as FreeSync, G-Sync Compatible or HDMI VRR. See: graphics.
  • VT-x / VMX - Intel's hardware virtualization feature. See: processors.
  • Vulkan - The modern cross-platform graphics and compute interface, used by most new Linux games and by DXVK and VKD3D-Proton. See: graphics.

W

  • WAN (wide area network) - the internet side of your router. See: network.
  • WGP (work-group processor) - Two compute units working as a pair on RDNA GPUs. ROCm OpenCL counts WGPs as compute units. See: graphics.
  • Whetstone - a classic floating-point (decimal maths) CPU benchmark. Its score is given in MWIPS. See: tools.
  • Wh (watt-hour) - energy used over time: 100 W for one hour is 100 Wh; 1,000 Wh is 1 kWh. See: User Guide 6.11.
  • Wine - A compatibility layer that runs Windows programs on Linux. See: graphics.
  • WMI - Windows Management Instrumentation; a way for firmware to offer vendor features through ACPI (PNP0C14 devices). See: machine, sensors.
  • WPA2 / WPA3 - Wi-Fi security standards; WPA3 is newer and stronger. See: network.
  • WPAD - Web Proxy Auto-Discovery, a way for a PC to find a PAC script automatically. See: network.
  • WPBT - Windows Platform Binary Table; lets firmware hand Windows a program to run at startup. See: machine.
  • WPD (Windows Portable Devices) - the Windows name for MTP/PTP devices such as phones and cameras. See: buses-2.
  • Wrap-around (counter) - a counter reaching its highest value and starting again from zero, like an odometer; SRS unwraps the CPU energy counter. See: User Guide 6.11.
  • Write-back cache - A drive feature that confirms a write once it is in the drive's own fast memory. See: storage.
  • WS-Discovery (Web Services Discovery) - the method modern Windows uses to find other PCs and printers on the LAN. See: network.
  • W (watt) - how fast power is being used right now. See: User Guide 6.11.
  • WWN - World Wide Name: a globally unique ID some drives report, used for stable device names. See: storage.

X

  • x86-64-v2 / v3 / v4 - CPU feature levels; v3 needs AVX2, v4 needs AVX-512. See: srs-items.
  • XDG autostart - the desktop standard: .desktop files in an autostart folder run at login. See: srs-items.
  • XDG (freedesktop.org Cross-Desktop Group) folders - the standard per-user folders such as ~/.config, ~/.local/share and ~/.cache. See: linux-os.
  • XFS - A high-performance Linux journaling filesystem. See: storage.
  • xHCI - The USB 3 host controller standard. One xHCI controller also serves USB 2 and USB 1 devices. See: buses-1, buses-2.
  • XMC (Switched Mezzanine Card) - an ANSI/VITA 42 plug-in module for industrial and embedded computers, connected over PCI Express. See: buses-2.
  • XMP - Intel Extreme Memory Profile; faster memory settings stored in the SPD. See: machine.
  • xxHash - a very fast non-cryptographic hash by Yann Collet, used to check data quickly; xxHash64 gives a 64-bit result. See: tools.

Z

  • zenergy - An out-of-tree Linux driver that reads AMD energy counters per core and per socket. See: sensors.
  • ZLUDA - A layer that lets programs written for NVIDIA CUDA run on AMD GPUs. See: graphics.
  • zram - a RAM-based block device that stores compressed data, often used as fast swap. See: linux-os, srs-items, storage.
  • Zstandard (zstd), LZ4, xz, zlib - common compression formats and libraries: lz4 is the fastest, zstd fast with good ratios, zlib (gzip / ZIP) the classic, and xz the smallest but slowest. See: tools.
  • zswap - a compressed cache in RAM that sits in front of disk swap. See: linux-os.
  • zx1 - HP's chipset for Itanium 2 servers and workstations. See: buses-2.
